# dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2

> Computes the modified LU factorization without pivoting of a real general M-by-N matrix (recursive kernel).

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlaorhrColGetrfnp2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2( order, M, N, A, LDA, d, strideD ) → integer
```

Computes the modified LU factorization without pivoting of a general M-by-N matrix (recursive kernel).

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, M )`; row-major requires `LDA ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of `A` |
| `d` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `d` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix to be factored. On exit, the factors L and U from the factorization $A-S=L \, U$; the unit diagonal elements of L are not stored.
- `d`: The diagonal elements of the diagonal M-by-N sign matrix S, $D(i) = S(i,i)$, where $1 \le i \le \min (M,N)$. The elements can be only plus or minus one.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, M )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2.ndarray(
    M, N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    D, strideD, offsetD
) → integer
```

Computes the modified LU factorization without pivoting of a real general M-by-N matrix `A` (recursive kernel).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `M` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `M ≥ 0` | number of rows of `A` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | number of columns of `A` |
| `A` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `M × N` |  | input/output matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `A` |
| `D` | `Float64Array` | out |  |  | output diagonal sign vector, length min(M,N) |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `D` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `D` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `M`: The number of rows of the matrix A. $M \ge 0$.
- `N`: The number of columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the M-by-N matrix to be factored. On exit, the factors L and U from the factorization $A-S=L \, U$; the unit diagonal elements of L are not stored.
- `D`: The diagonal elements of the diagonal M-by-N sign matrix S, $D(i) = S(i,i)$, where $1 \le i \le \min (M,N)$. The elements can be only plus or minus one.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `min( M, N ) === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLAORHR_COL_GETRFNP2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2.f).
-   The factorization has the form `A - S = L * U` where `S` is an `M`-by-`N` diagonal sign matrix with diagonal `D`, `L` is `M`-by-`N` lower triangular with unit diagonal, and `U` is `M`-by-`N` upper triangular. The diagonal `D[i] = -sign(A[i,i])` is computed at each elimination step so that the pivot is at least one in absolute value, guaranteeing numerical stability without row interchanges.
-   This routine is used by the Householder reconstruction routine `dorhr_col`.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
/* eslint-disable camelcase */

import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2';

const M = 3;
const N = 3;

const A = new Float64Array( [ 0.5, 0.3, -0.2, -0.4, 0.6, 0.1, 0.2, -0.1, 0.7 ] );
const D = new Float64Array( 3 );

dlaorhr_col_getrfnp2( 'column-major', M, N, A, M, D, 1 );
console.log( A ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( D ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLAORHR_COL_GETRFNP2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLAORHR\_COL\_GETRFNP2 computes the modified LU factorization without pivoting of a real general M-by-N matrix A. The factorization has the form:

$$
A - S = L \, U
$$

where:

-   S is a m-by-n diagonal sign matrix with the diagonal D, so that
-   $D(i) = S(i,i)$, $1 \le i \le \min (M,N)$. The diagonal D is constructed
-   as $D(i)=-\mathrm{SIGN}(A(i,i))$, where `A(i,i)` is the value after performing
-   i-1 steps of Gaussian elimination. This means that the diagonal
-   element at each step of "modified" Gaussian elimination is at
-   least one in absolute value (so that division-by-zero not
-   possible during the division by the diagonal element);

L is a M-by-N lower triangular matrix with unit diagonal elements (lower trapezoidal if $M > N$);

and U is a M-by-N upper triangular matrix (upper trapezoidal if $M < N$).

This routine is an auxiliary routine used in the Householder reconstruction routine DORHR\_COL. In DORHR\_COL, this routine is applied to an M-by-N matrix A with orthonormal columns, where each element is bounded by one in absolute value. With the choice of the matrix S above, one can show that the diagonal element at each step of Gaussian elimination is the largest (in absolute value) in the column on or below the diagonal, so that no pivoting is required for numerical stability \[1\].

For more details on the Householder reconstruction algorithm, including the modified LU factorization, see \[1\].

This is the recursive version of the LU factorization algorithm. Denote A - S by B. The algorithm divides the matrix B into four submatrices:

```text
    [  B11 | B12  ]  where B11 is n1 by n1,
B = [ -----|----- ]        B21 is (m-n1) by n1,
    [  B21 | B22  ]        B12 is n1 by n2,
                           B22 is (m-n1) by n2,
                           with n1 = min(m,n)/2, n2 = n-n1.
```

The subroutine calls itself to factor B11, solves for B21, solves for B12, updates B22, then calls itself to factor B22.

For more details on the recursive LU algorithm, see \[2\].

DLAORHR\_COL\_GETRFNP2 is called to factorize a block by the blocked routine DLAORHR\_COL\_GETRFNP, which uses blocked code calling Level 3 BLAS to update the submatrix. However, DLAORHR\_COL\_GETRFNP2 is self-sufficient and can be used without DLAORHR\_COL\_GETRFNP.

\[1\] "Reconstructing Householder vectors from tall-skinny QR",

-   G. Ballard, J. Demmel, L. Grigori, M. Jacquelin, H.D. Nguyen,
-   E. Solomonik, J. Parallel Distrib. Comput.,
-   vol. 85, pp. 3-31, 2015.

\[2\] "Recursion leads to automatic variable blocking for dense linear

-   algebra algorithms", F. Gustavson, IBM J. of Res. and Dev.,
-   vol. 41, no. 6, pp. 737-755, 1997.

</section>
